category_title: Students with academic anxiety who use physical gestures to communicate emerging conceptual understanding
scenario_title: Negative exponent problem and reciprocal concept
minimal_context: Luke is working on a math problem involving negative exponents with his tutor and a peer, trying to get rid of a negative exponent in the denominator.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at this negative exponent problem. Try to get rid of the negative exponent in the denominator.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I worked on this one by myself, but I can't figure out how to solve it.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: If you want to get rid of the negative exponent in the denominator and make it one number, you have to multiply by the reciprocal. Do you remember what that is?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Can you explain what you mean by that?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Uh…The same thing, but twist, right? (He responds in an unsure, questioning way, twisting his hand back and forth in a circular motion with his palm facing toward the tutor, looking self-conscious about answering in front of his peer.)

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Let's look at this negative exponent problem. Try to get rid of the negative exponent in the denominator.

STUDENT: I worked on this one by myself, but I can't figure out how to solve it.

TUTOR: If you want to get rid of the negative exponent in the denominator and make it one number, you have to multiply by the reciprocal. Do you remember what that is?

STUDENT: When you switch right?

TUTOR: Can you explain what you mean by that?

STUDENT: Uh…The same thing, but twist, right? (He responds in an unsure, questioning way, twisting his hand back and forth in a circular motion with his palm facing toward the tutor, looking self-conscious about answering in front of his peer.)

task.content: Solving negative exponent problems, specifically how to get rid of a negative exponent in the denominator and make it one number by multiplying by the reciprocal

context.social_setting: Working with a tutor (Matt) and a peer (Henry) who was also school-identified as a student with LD in math and reading

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: After working independently on a problem but not being able to figure out how to solve it, and being asked by the tutor 'Do you remember what that is?' regarding a reciprocal
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Responded in an unsure, questioning way while TWISTING his hand back and forth in a circular motion with his palm facing toward the tutor
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Struggled with academic anxiety and was especially self-conscious about appearing incompetent in front of his peers
related_quotes: Uh…The same thing, but twist, right?

behavior_patterns.condition: When lacking the formal mathematical terminology to explain a concept
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Uses physical gestures, such as TWISTING his hand back and forth in a circular motion, to communicate his emerging conceptual understanding
related_quotes: It is when you flip the numbers
